fields.h1: Build a Massage Booking Form for Studios and Mobile Therapists
fields.hero_description: Build a massage booking form that matches each session to a free therapist and room, then saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: The Schedule Behind Every Massage Session
fields.features_subheading: A massage booking form is only as good as the times it offers. Emergent builds the form and the schedule it reads from.
fields.feature_1:
Start times that fit the session

A 90-minute massage needs 90 open minutes in a therapist's day, plus the cleanup time you set after it. The form shows only the start times where the whole session fits.
fields.feature_2:
A named therapist or first available

Clients can pick a therapist by name or choose first available. First available books whoever is free soonest, and the confirmation names the therapist the client got.
fields.feature_3:
Rooms counted with therapists

Tell the form how many treatment rooms you have. A time appears only if it has an open room as well as an open therapist, so a time with no empty room stays off the list.
fields.feature_4:
A cancellation policy agreed at booking

Show your notice period above the submit button and make the client tick a box to accept it. When someone cancels inside that window, the app marks the booking as late.
fields.feature_5:
Waitlist offers sent by email

When a session opens up, the app emails the first client on the waitlist a link to claim it. If the time runs out before they claim it, the offer moves to the next name.
fields.feature_6:
Your booking code on GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building on it. Bookings and package balances stay in a database you own, with no response caps.

fields.usecase_heading: Booking Rules From Four Massage Practices
fields.tab_content_1:
From a 1 p.m. visit, the next opening is 3:15

Zuri Vandemark drives to every session she books for Bluecreek Mobile Massage, and she keeps 45 minutes of road time between home visits. Romilly Prowse in Easton Ridge enters her street address and books a 90-minute visit at 1 p.m. The form now offers 3:15 p.m. as Zuri's next start time that day.
fields.tab_content_2:
No room at 5:30 when Kasimir and Solveig hold both

Osprey Lane Bodywork runs three therapists through two rooms. On Tuesday at 5:30 p.m. both rooms are in use by clients of Kasimir Dunleavy and Solveig Ravel. The form leaves 5:30 off the list even though Isolde Quint is free. Hesper Doane picks first available and gets Isolde at 6:30 p.m., when room 2 opens up.
fields.tab_content_3:
A slot freed by a late cancellation goes to Anwen

Thimbleberry Massage asks clients for 24 hours of notice, and nobody books without ticking the policy box. A client cancels a Friday 4 p.m. session at 8 p.m. Thursday, 20 hours ahead, and it is marked a late cancellation. Anwen Feeney is first of 3 on the waitlist. The app emails her with 2 hours to claim it.
fields.tab_content_4:
By visit 4, Daria has 1 visit left on her package

Daria Ashbury bought a 5-visit package at Hollbrook Massage in January. Each booking she makes takes one visit off her balance, and the balance sits on her client record. When she books visit 4, her package shows 1 visit left, and the app emails her that 1 visit remains.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Massage Booking Form
fields.howto_description: Work out what a massage booking form should offer and when, then build it with Emergent and test it in seven steps.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down every session you sell
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Count your rooms and your drive time
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write the policy in one sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: List each session length you offer, such as 60 and 90 minutes, plus any add-on that adds time. Note the cleanup time a room needs after each session. Those numbers decide which start times the form can show.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down who gives which session and the hours each therapist works. A therapist who does not offer hot stone should never appear for it. Clients who pick first available then see only therapists who give the session they chose.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Note how many treatment rooms you can book at once. If you also visit clients at home, set the drive time to keep between visits and enter each ZIP code you serve. The form checks both before it offers a time.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick a notice period for cancellations and say what happens when a client cancels inside it. Place that sentence above the submit button with a required checkbox. Every client then agrees to the same wording you point to later.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the form to Emergent in one prompt, using the sessions, therapists, rooms, and policy from your notes. You get the booking form along with the database that stores every booking. Ask in plain English when a session or a rule needs to change.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add a waitlist and package balances
fields.howto_step_6_des: Let clients join a waitlist when a day is full, and set how long an emailed offer stays open before it moves to the next name. If you sell packages, keep the visits each client has left on their record.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book a test session that starts later today from your phone and cancel it an hour later. It should be marked late, and the first test name on your waitlist should get the emailed offer. Claim it from that inbox to see the slot booked again.

faq_plan.q: What is a massage booking form?
faq_plan.a: A massage booking form is the page a client uses to book a session. They choose a session length, a therapist and a time, then accept your cancellation policy. Behind it, the form checks therapist hours and free rooms before it offers a time.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a massage booking form?
faq_plan.a: List your sessions, therapists, rooms, and cancellation policy first. Then describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form and the database behind it. Book a test session yourself before you share the link with clients.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a massage booking form include?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the client's name, email and phone, then the session length, a therapist or first available, and the date and time. Add a required checkbox for your cancellation policy. Leave health questions to a separate intake step to keep booking short.

faq_plan.q: Should a massage booking form count rooms as well as therapists?
faq_plan.a: Yes, whenever you have fewer treatment rooms than therapists on shift. A hotel booking form counts rooms night by night. A massage form counts them hour by hour, next to each therapist's schedule, and hides any time with no room free.

faq_plan.q: How do I add a cancellation policy to a massage booking form?
faq_plan.a: State the notice period and what happens inside it in one sentence, such as 24 hours or the session counts as late, and make accepting it required. Save the policy wording with each booking. If you change the policy later, you can still see which version a client agreed to.

faq_plan.q: How should a massage booking form pick who gets a waitlist opening?
faq_plan.a: Offer it to the first name on the list, with a set time to claim it, and move it to the next name if that time runs out. A strict order is simple to explain to any client who asks why they missed a slot. Once a client books, take them off the list before the next offer goes out.

faq_plan.q: Can a massage booking form handle home visits?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for the street address and limit home visits to the ZIP codes you travel to, with a message for anyone outside them. The same rule works on any booking form that sends someone to the customer. Add a field for parking notes or a gate code as well.

faq_plan.q: How do session packages work on a massage booking form?
faq_plan.a: Each client's package is stored with the visits left, and every booking takes one off. Decide what the form shows at zero, such as single sessions or a note to buy a new package. Emergent keeps every balance in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should a massage booking form let clients choose their therapist?
faq_plan.a: Yes, and offer first available next to the names. Returning clients can pick the therapist they know, while new clients get the soonest time. Add a one-line bio under each name, such as the techniques that therapist trained in, to help a new client choose.

faq_plan.q: Can I copy my massage booking form for a different service?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask Emergent to copy the form and describe what changes, since it builds and edits forms from a prompt. A dj booking form, for example, books a whole evening and a venue instead of a 60-minute session and a room.

plan.angle: There is no ranked top 10 for this query, and the AlsoAsked pull returned only tipping and etiquette questions. The page wins by treating the massage booking form as a scheduling tool rather than a contact form: it offers only times when a therapist, a room or the drive actually allows a session, it holds a cancellation policy the client agrees to, and it keeps the waitlist and package counts in one table. Health and consent questions belong to the massage intake page, so this page stays on the booking itself.

findings.quote: Book a test session for tomorrow from your phone and cancel it an hour later. It should be marked late
findings.issue: With a 24-hour notice period, a session tomorrow booked in the morning for a late slot is more than 24 hours away, so it would not be marked late; the expected result is stated as certain.
findings.fix: Book a test session that starts within your notice period (for example, a few hours from now) and cancel it.

findings.field: faq item 6 vs feature_5, tab_content_3, howto_step_6
findings.quote: An opening then goes to the first person whose answers fit it, instead of the first name on the list.
findings.issue: Feature 5 ('emails the first client on the waitlist'), tab 3 ('Anwen Feeney is first of 3 on the waitlist') and step 6 ('moves to the next name') describe first-in-line; FAQ 6 recommends against first-in-line. Both can be configured, but the page reads as arguing with itself.
findings.fix: Frame FAQ 6 as an option: 'By default the first name gets it; ask for days and therapists if you want the first person whose answers fit.'

findings.quote: list the towns you travel to / limit home visits to the ZIP codes you travel to
findings.issue: The service-area rule is towns in step 3 and ZIP codes in FAQ 7 (HUB_RULES 2a consistency: same term for the same thing).
findings.fix: Pick one (ZIP codes) and use it in both.
